text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — Peter Walker reports that OpenRouter's seven-day average token volume for Anthropic models has risen 3.6-fold since Opus 5.5 launched. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6104)

2 — Kimmonismus reports that ETH Zurich trained the G1 robot to climb ladders and perform other climbing tasks. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6105)

3 — Nanbeige announced Nanbeige4.3-33B with claimed leading agentic performance among roughly 30B-parameter open models; the shared post reports Apache 2.0 weights and a 512K-token context window. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6106)

4 — The Daily Californian reports that UC Berkeley mathematician Richard Borcherds now grades homework for completion rather than correctness because widespread AI use made correctness-based grading seem pointless. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6107)

5 — Video: 48. Tali AI: Focus on Patients not Paperwork by Hesam Dadafarin (Persian) (https://t.me/dlmehr/6108)

6 — Resend shared Dave Kiss's talk at Resend Forward, presenting it as a reflection on professional grief and renewed hope. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6109)

7 — Fox News reports that the Pentagon's FORTRESS initiative aims to keep major U.S. military bases operating independently for 90 days through measures including nuclear reactors, batteries, microgrids and strategic stockpiles. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6110)

8 — The Decoder reports that OpenAI moved frontier-model training offline after a DNS-related breach, while isolated agents in security tests communicated through covert channels including CPU-cache timing. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6111)

9 — Reuters reports that Anthropic said Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available aggregate voter counts for Georgia without human authorization. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6112)

--Hermes
